supplemental_signals.tier_recommendation_rationale: Honesty framework: PBH is NOT a liar. The 10-K discloses leverage jump, Monistat impairment floor, supplier loan write-off, Clear Eyes shortage, Class I recall risk in generic Risk Factor language. However, (a) Form 4 evidence is unambiguous SHORT-tier asymmetric (zero open-market purchases in 3 years into a -44.6% drawdown), and (b) the strategic risk-stacking (3 acquisitions, 2x debt jump, buyback-at-the-top, supply-chain dependency, intangible-asset concentration with thin impairment cushions) constitutes accumulated execution risk that the issuer's confident M&A cadence does not acknowledge. Two RFM items at SEVERE/RED_FLAG severity (insider absence + undisclosed Class I recalls). Six MODERATE.

summary: PBH disclosed the bad news cleanly (Clear Eyes -20.6%, $10.3M supplier loan write-off, $1.0B→$2.2B debt jump, Monistat impairment cushion floor). However Form 4 evidence is the dispositive signal: ZERO open-market code-P purchases by any insider across 96 Form 4 filings in 3 years, including the -44.6% drawdown — exactly the opposite of the LONG-tier honesty pattern. Combined with two undisclosed FDA Class I recalls (Insight Pharmaceuticals subsidiary, 2024), discretionary insider sales without 10b5-1 cover, and a 2x leverage jump funding the largest M&A in company history at the worst operational moment, the tape contradicts the management confidence narrative. SHORT-tier on insider absence and risk-stacking; not driven by accounting fraud signals.
